judged_text: Negative values of limit or offset (params[:limit].to_i / params[:offset].to_i) are passed unvalidated into .limit(-1).offset(-1), which Postgres rejects ('LIMIT/OFFSET must not be negative'), producing an unhandled 500. Any anonymous or regular user can trigger a 500 with a crafted query string (e.g. ?offset=-1), generating error noise and log volume; the contract should return a 4xx for malformed pagination input.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination params are used directly: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then applied as `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no validation or clamping to non-negative values, so a request like `?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` can produce `.offset(-1)`/`.limit(-1)`, which can raise a Postgres error (500) instead of returning a 4xx. This behavior is verifiably possible from the diff and is reachable by regular users hitting the public `/groups/:group_id/members` endpoint.
